To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the data driven recursive least squares estimation for model predictive current control of permanent magnet synchronous motors improves the control performance during steady state and transients.

the proposed data driven estimation scheme is capable of compensating WB model deviations and that the resulting MPC controller is able to improve the control quality of a permanent magnet machine in a self commissioning drive.

a) a data driven recursive least squares estimation algorithm for the current control is a promising approach for compensating for the WB plant model inaccuracies and b) the proposed algorithm improves the control performance significantly during transients and at steady state, especially in the presence of saturation effects and inverter interlocking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a data driven, model based MPC for the current control.
the improvement of MPC control performance for electric drive systems during the self commissioning process and the exploitation of the full potential of MPC in industrial applications.
the development of a data driven, recursive least squares based estimation method for model predictive current control of permanent magnet synchronous motors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach is a promising candidate for the control of electric drives with a high dynamic behavior, e.g. in the area of traction, aerospace and marine drives.
the presented approach is a promising solution for the current control in self commissioning drives.
the proposed data driven approach is superior to the conventional WB approach in the sense of control performance, flexibility and robustness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed data driven recursive least squares estimation scheme for the current control is able to significantly improve the control performance in the case of modeling uncertainties.
the proposed data driven approach can be used to improve the performance of a FCS MPC in terms of torque and current ripples and, consequently, the torque and current ripple indices.
the presented data driven approach allows for an improved control performance in the presence of modeling errors and, therefore, a more accurate control of the permanent magnet synchronous motor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
data driven modeling is a promising tool to overcome the drawbacks of WB modeling in MPC.
a data driven approach can be successfully used in the field of model predictive control of electric drives, where WB modeling is typically used.
the presented data driven approach is a promising alternative to the WB modeling paradigm in electric drive control.
